title: HW matrix throughput and cost-per-token analysis for inference load harness
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Run a standardized tokens/sec and latency (p95) benchmarking sweep across target GPU types (A10, L4, A100, H100) and produce a reproducible cost-per-token report for the inference runtime. This ticket covers: (1) defining test workloads and sequence mixes, (2) harmonizing harness configs and billing calculations, (3) running clusterized sweeps, (4) automated regression detection rules, and (5) drafting a consolidated results and recommendations doc.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Benchmark harness can run identical job definition across GPU types via a single CLI/config file. 2) We produce a CSV with tokens/sec, p95 latency, and effective cost-per-1k-tokens for each GPU and model variant. 3) Alerting rules for 10% regressions in tokens/sec or 15% regressions in p95 are checked-in to prometheus/rules repo as PR. 4) Draft with suggestions for default production GPU choices added to runtime playbook.
test_plan:
- Workloads: short-chat (avg seq 64), standard-completion (avg seq 512), long-context (avg seq 4096).
- Models: mainline 13B fp16, 7B quantized, and a 70B factory default where capacity allows.
- Metrics: sustained tokens/sec (30s sliding window), p95 end-to-end decode latency, GPU utilization, memory headroom, queue depth.
- Harness: k6+python driver (internal load-generator) with exact tokenization via tokenizer API to ensure tokens/sec parity.
- Batching: test batch sizes [1,4,8,16] where supported; test KV cache warm/cold states.
- Repeat: 3 runs per config, median-of-3 selected; run at target QPS to saturate but not OOM the instance.
- Cost calc: use per-hour GPU price (spot and on-demand), normalized to per-1k-tokens by dividing hourly cost by tokens/sec * 3600 / 1000.
- Output: CSV + per-GPU markdown summary and Grafana dashboard links.
harness_details: We standardized harness interface as: ./bench --config <yaml> --target-gpu <A10|L4|A100|H100> --model <path|catalog> --seq-profile <short|standard|long> --batch <n>. The harness records raw token timestamps so p95 is computed client-side to avoid sampling bias. Warmup phase is 120s to populate KV cache where applicable. Runs emit metrics to prometheus pushgateway and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/ENG-12840/.
cost_assumptions: On-demand hourly prices used for initial report (internal discount applied in notes): A10: $0.95/hr, L4: $1.25/hr, A100: $3.20/hr, H100: $6.00/hr. These are placeholders; finance provided a reference rate card in spreadsheet link. We compute cost-per-1k-tokens = (hourly_price) / (tokens_per_sec * 3600 / 1000). Spot runs annotated separately in CSV.
results_summary:
(median-of-3 runs, standard-completion profile, batch=8, KV cache warm):
- A10: tokens/sec = 3,200; p95 latency = 210ms; cost-per-1k-tokens = $0.00029
- L4: tokens/sec = 3,900; p95 latency = 180ms; cost-per-1k-tokens = $0.00018
- A100: tokens/sec = 10,800; p95 latency = 95ms; cost-per-1k-tokens = $0.00008
- H100: tokens/sec = 20,400; p95 latency = 48ms; cost-per-1k-tokens = $0.000083
Notes: H100 has best raw throughput but A100 provides strongest price/perf with current price assumptions. L4 shows excellent latency for small-medium batch sizes and is attractive for latency-sensitive PLG tiers. A10 is cost-effective for low-throughput dev fleets. These numbers are intentionally computed from the practical harness (including RPC overhead) rather than micro-bench kernels to reflect production economics.
regression_detection: Implemented two complementary signals: (1) tokens/sec drop: alert if 10% sustained drop in rolling 1h median vs. baseline for the same config; (2) p95 latency increase: alert if p95 rises 15% vs. baseline. Baselines are stored as taggable artifacts per model+gpu+batch+seq-profile. Detection logic lives in prometheus alert rules (file bench-regressions.yml) + a smoke-check workflow that runs nightly sweep on a small representative batch and files ENG tickets when triggered. We included auto-triage labels and a reproduction script that re-runs the failing config in isolated staging.

next_steps: 1) Validate spot pricing recalculation and re-run long-context profile on A100/H100 for 70B model. 2) Merge prometheus rules PR and schedule nightly smoke-run. 3) Add an automated table to the console runtime playbook showing recommended default GPU per workload. 4) Coordinate with finance before publishing public-facing cost numbers.
